findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concrete opt-in mechanism for overlap judging (e.g. a named parameter on the plan-review entry point) so 'requested' vs 'not requested' is an executable switch.
evidence: 'Overlap judging is opt-in per run. A plan review that does not ask for it...'
ACs say 'With overlap judging requested' / 'not requested' but no section defines HOW a caller requests it
findings.finding: The opt-in mechanism by which overlap judging is 'requested' is never specified; ACs reference 'overlap judging requested' / 'not requested' states but the plan never names the switch (a parameter to the review entry point, a CLI flag, a config key).
findings.location: Approach, 'On demand, not on every review'; ACs 1,5,6,7
scenarios: Executor must decide whether to add a function parameter, a CLI flag, or a config toggle to invoke overlap judging

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the diagnostic's shape and recording channel (e.g. a non-blocking diagnostic record on the review result keyed to the degradation cause) so each 'diagnostic recorded' AC has an observable target.
evidence: 'overlap judging is skipped with a diagnostic'
AC: 'a test asserting the diagnostic is present, with the overlap finding set empty' — 'present' in what artifact is undefined
findings.finding: The 'diagnostic' recorded when retrieval degrades has no specified shape or recording channel. Two ACs assert 'a diagnostic naming the absent index is recorded in place of an overlap finding' but never say where it is recorded (a special finding kind, a log line, a result field) or how a test retrieves it.
findings.location: ACs: 'a diagnostic naming the absent index is recorded', 'a diagnostic naming the catch-up failure is recorded'
scenarios: A test must assert the diagnostic is present but the plan does not say which field/artifact to inspect

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the data path from find_similar's new failure signal to a deterministic, test-queryable diagnostic record in the plan-review output (e.g. an INDETERMINATE-style diagnostic entry in the findings list), separate from the LLM-interpreted extra_context string.
evidence: Plan: 'The change is an opt-in diagnostic signal on the existing function' — describes find_similar's return/signal, not the plan-review-side recording
_chunk_extra_context returns a plain string joined into LLM context (pass1.py:215-223); a string fed to the finder is not a deterministic recorded diagnostic
AC: 'a sidecar test asserting the diagnostic is present, with the overlap finding set empty' — implies a structured diagnostic distinct from the findings list and distinct from LLM output
findings.finding: The plan requires a deterministic recorded diagnostic (absent-index / catch-up-failure) asserted by tests as present 'in place of an overlap finding', but the only described injection path into plan review is the LLM-interpreted extra_context string; the plan does not specify how find_similar's new diagnostic signal becomes a structured, test-queryable diagnostic record in the plan-review output.
findings.location: Approach: 'The one gap is failure distinguishability' + ACs 'a diagnostic naming the absent index is recorded in place of an overlap finding' / 'a diagnostic naming the catch-up failure is recorded'
scenarios: Index absent: the finder receives no candidates in extra_context, but there is no specified place for the 'names the absent index' diagnostic to be recorded for the test to assert
Catch-up raises: find_similar returns [] (indistinguishable from empty match today); the ticket adds a signal, but the plan never routes that signal into a recorded plan-review diagnostic

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the diagnostic signal's shape/vocabulary that find_similar (or the overlap retrieval wrapper) returns to distinguish absent-index vs catch-up-failure vs matched-nothing, and name the plan-review output slot (e.g. a coverage key) where the overlap diagnostic is recorded in place of a finding.
evidence: Plan: 'The change is an opt-in diagnostic signal on the existing function' — names no shape/vocabulary

find_similar currently collapses all three modes to [] (src/rebar/similar/__init__.py:63-64 absent, :67-72 catch-up fail, :83-85 other); the plan requires a signal separating them but defines none of the discriminating values
ACs demand a diagnostic 'naming the absent index' vs 'naming the catch-up failure' as DISTINCT recorded artifacts, yet the plan specifies no field/enum carrying that distinction

Existing plan-review diagnostics are merged into coverage via coverage_extra (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py:140); the plan does not state the overlap diagnostic is recorded there or in any named finding/coverage slot, so the two 'naming' ACs have no defined assertion target
findings.finding: The 'diagnostic signal' the ticket adds to find_similar to distinguish absent-index / catch-up-failure / matched-nothing is referenced by four acceptance criteria but its value vocabulary and its recording location in the plan-review output are never defined.
findings.location: Approach — 'The one gap is failure distinguishability'; ACs 'When the index is absent, a diagnostic naming the absent index is recorded' and 'When catch-up raises, a diagnostic naming the catch-up failure is recorded'
scenarios: Executor implements find_similar's diagnostic return and cannot tell what discriminated values the two 'naming' ACs expect
Test author for the absent-index vs catch-up-failure ACs has no specified field to assert the diagnostic text/kind against
findings.suggested_fix: Specify a small closed set of diagnostic kinds (e.g. 'index-absent', 'catch-up-failed') with human text, returned alongside the candidate list, and state they are recorded under a named key in coverage (as coverage_extra in claimability.py already does) so the two 'naming' ACs assert against a defined field.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion for the provider-error degradation: the review completes with its normal verdict and a diagnostic naming the provider failure is recorded in place of an overlap finding.
evidence: 'When the index is absent, catch-up fails, or the configured embedding provider errors, overlap judging is skipped with a diagnostic'
ACs cover 'index is absent' and 'catch-up raises' with diagnostic + verdict assertions; no AC covers the provider-error degradation
findings.finding: The Approach lists three degradation modes (index absent, catch-up fails, configured embedding provider errors) but acceptance criteria give diagnostic/normal-verdict ACs only for the first two. The provider-error path is a described failure point with no covering criterion.
findings.location: Approach 'Degradation matches the sibling's'; AC set (index-absent and catch-up-raises have ACs, provider-error does not)
scenarios: Embedding tier configured but provider returns an error during the overlap query

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a criterion (or state the contract) that find_similar's existing behaviour — return value and 'Never raises' property — is unchanged for callers that do not opt into the diagnostic signal.
evidence: 'The change is an opt-in diagnostic signal on the existing function, not a parallel retrieval entry point.'
find_similar is 'the package's whole surface' (:8) and has an existing create-time caller; no AC asserts that caller is unaffected
findings.finding: The plan modifies the shared public function find_similar (adding an opt-in diagnostic signal) but never states the backward-compat guarantee for its existing create-time caller. The checkpoint-identity AC protects only the plan-review path, not find_similar's existing contract ('Never raises', collapse-to-[] at :55).
findings.location: Approach 'The one gap is failure distinguishability...is what this ticket adds to the retrieval surface'
scenarios: Create-time surfacing continues calling find_similar after this change

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the create-path consumer `src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:196` and specify that the `find_similar` diagnostic signal is added as a default-valued keyword (opt-in) so its return shape and that call site remain byte-identical.
evidence: `src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:27` imports `from rebar.similar import find_similar`; `:196-201` invokes it on the ticket-create advisory path

The plan asserts opt-in behaviour only for the plan-review path ('a plan review that does not ask for it … its checkpoint identity is unchanged'); it says nothing about the create-path caller's compatibility with the signature change

The module docstring (__init__.py:8-11) names create-time as a live caller: 'consulted on the write path of ticket creation, where an advisory that raised would turn a successful create into a failed command'
findings.finding: The plan modifies the shared `find_similar` surface ('an opt-in diagnostic signal on the existing function') but does not enumerate its create-path consumer `src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:196`, which calls `find_similar(str(tracker), title=..., description=..., exclude_id=...)` outside both `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` and `src/rebar/similar/`.
findings.location: Approach — 'The one gap is failure distinguishability … an opt-in diagnostic signal on the existing function'
scenarios: The diagnostic is added by changing find_similar's return shape (e.g. results+diagnostic tuple) rather than a new default keyword, silently breaking the recent_creates create-path call that expects a bare list
findings.suggested_fix: State that the diagnostic is surfaced via a new default-valued keyword parameter (e.g. `diagnostics=None`) leaving the return type and the existing `recent_creates.py` call unchanged, and add an AC asserting the create-path call's result is unchanged.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly whether overlap judging rides the existing G5/injection chunk's single finder call (0 added calls; 'the judge' = that chunk's finder) or is a dedicated overlap-judge unit with its own ≤2-call budget, and reconcile the 'passed to the judge' / '≤2 LLM calls' criteria with the 'no new pass / unchanged identity when not requested' claim.
evidence: Plan: 'Appending candidates there rather than adding a pass keeps checkpoint identity, caching, resumption working unchanged'
Plan: 'A plan review that does not ask for it spends 0 additional calls' — consistent with riding an existing finder call, not with a 2-call judge
AC: 'At most 2 LLM calls are made for overlap judging' and 'At most 10 candidates are passed to the judge'

pass1.py has no existing 'judge' unit (search for 'judge' returns no matches); _chunk_extra_context (pass1.py:215-223) feeds the EXISTING chunk finder, which issues the chunk's normal call, not a dedicated overlap call
findings.finding: The plan describes overlap judging both as riding an existing Pass-1 chunk's extra_context (adding 0 LLM calls, which is what makes the unchanged-identity/zero-cost criteria hold) and as a separate 'judge' with a 2-call budget and a 'candidates passed to the judge' boundary; these are structurally incompatible and the plan never says which one is built.
findings.location: Approach: 'Ride the existing Pass-1 extra-context seam' + ACs 'At most 10 candidates are passed to the judge' / 'At most 2 LLM calls are made for overlap judging'
scenarios: Implementer appends candidates to extra_context and the '2 LLM calls for overlap judging' criterion has no call to count (the finder call is the chunk's, not an overlap call)
Implementer builds a dedicated 2-call judge unit, contradicting 'rather than adding a pass' and risking a new checkpoint unit that changes identity/topology
